concerns: Density at the floor. 3,935 prose words against a 4,600 target — inside the band by 25 words, and the thinnest thing in the chapter is the thing the card names first: 'Treswick anatomized from inside'. The city is anatomized well in two places (L21's bench and its three walks; L71's whole machine seen from above) and nowhere else. If F-002's 793-word Cleon opening is cut back, the recovered words belong to the ascent (F-008) and to the city, not to new material.

Vastin's forty years against his fifty-three. L57 'A man who had stood in front of clerks for forty years on the far side of the counter' would have him entering Compact service at thirteen, given the age correction recorded in STATE_RUNNING ('Vastin is FIFTY-THREE (fifty-one at B6 Ch14; ~sixteen months)'). This is NOT a Ch9 defect and should not be repaired here: 'forty years' is established across the drafted book (ch02 ×4, ch03 ×3, ch05, ch06, ch10, ch11, ch12, ch13, ch15, ch16, ch17, ch19). Raising to planning as a series-level reconciliation — either the age or the span has to move, and it has to move everywhere at once.

ch08.md is still unrepaired against ruling 16. The previous chapter carries four mule references and 'the mule's chair', where the ruling states the mule went north with Oryn on the 281st and the inn's chair is 'a chair nobody sat in'. DECISIONS row 16 lists Ch8 as 'repaired 2026-09-05' but the file on disk does not reflect it. Ch9 is clean; the seam behind it is not.

'A careful man' as a refrain. Seven instances of 'careful man'/'careful young man' inside roughly 600 words at L43–L61. It is doing real work — the clerk's care is the exposure and the machine's gap at once — but at seven it stops characterising him and starts announcing the theme. Two or three cuts would sharpen it. Below the charter's cap, so recorded as taste, not as a finding.

The counter — the packet's named turn — is staged at one remove, from the lane, with the strata-talk audible only as 'the shape of them' plus one sentence through a door. I judge this the right call rather than a defect: Cael cannot be at that counter, the POV holds, and the clerk stepping into the yard door to make the count with his pen puts the actual turn in Cael's sight. Recorded so a repair pass does not 'fix' it by moving the camera indoors.

'"Noted," Karis said' (L17) sits close to modern register — it reads as a receipt rather than as this character's speech. Not modern idiom in the strict sense and Karis is a woman who files things, so it is defensible; flagged for the line pass only.

'become something they haven't seen' (L75) drops the 'yet' the canonical line carries in both Book 5/6 ('I want to become something they haven't seen yet') and B7 Ch4 ('I told them I wanted to become something they hadn't seen yet'). The Ch9 card itself quotes it short, so the draft is following the card; noting it so the series' most-repeated Lira line does not erode by attrition.
strengths: The machine is dramatised, not explained. The clerk's not-asking at L47–L53 is the chapter's best writing: the pen making the count 'one two three four', the eye stopping half a breath on Brom's shoulder 'because a careful man's eye goes to the thing that is carried wrong', the trouble arriving on his face, and then Karis's voice coming through the door mid-argument and deciding it for him. The gap in the form is shown as a young man wanting an hour to end. Do not compress this.

L61 pays Ch8's log exactly and without underlining: 'The bar had not been lifted. It had not been consulted. It had stood where it always stood, on a form in an office in the west, and this form, in this office, had had no column for it.' The payoff line at L63 — '*That's the door*, he had written. It was. It was a young man wanting an hour to end.' — is three sentences and does not explain itself.

Lira's want lands on behaviour, not statement. 'And he saw it not pull' (L81), then the physical proof in the vocabulary Cael has used for her for four books — 'the set of her shoulders, the weight going forward, the thing in her that had been built to climb' — and then the weight not going forward. She says almost nothing and writes nothing. This is the obligation met in the series' own register.

The three held breaths at L55–L59 are the chapter's cleanest piece of character work: Cael's out, Lira's a count later 'on purpose, so that it was hers and not his', and Vastin's never held at all because he has stood on the other side of that counter for a career. Three people priced in one beat, none of them explained.

Vastin's consent at L35 is exactly the right size — 'had said, "Yes," in the ledger voice, before anyone could ask it aloud' — and the reflex is held for Ch10 without being teased. 'The finding out was not this morning's' is a plant, not a wink.

The closing image delivers the card: the door older than the walls because the walls were quarried from behind it (L95), 'the one level of the city where rank had run out, because the stone was older than rank and had never been told about it' (L97), and the last clause, 'and the tiers closed, and the dark opened' (L103). The file ends there, with no log and no dialogue. Whatever F-003 changes about who closes the door, this ending survives it.

The promise is kept and costed rather than announced: the lane behind the office, Seln's 'left and left and left again, keeping the square on the far side of a row of houses the whole way', the square reduced to 'light between buildings', and the price named — 'the not-setting-foot had cost the four of them a longer walk with boxes and had been done without a word, because a thing written in a log at a fire was a thing the crew had read too' (L31).
